findings.claim: total() now raises KeyError for line items without a qty field
findings.failure_scenario: A cart built by the legacy checkout sends items as {"price": 10}. total() evaluates i["qty"] and raises KeyError, so the order page returns 500.

citations.quote: return sum(i["price"] * i["qty"] for i in items)

findings.verdict_reason: The base commit summed prices only; nothing in the diff adds qty to older callers.

fix.description: Default the quantity to 1 when it is missing.
fix.patch_sketch: return sum(i["price"] * i.get("qty", 1) for i in items)

premises.statement: Items without qty mean a quantity of one
total() is the only caller that reads qty

open_questions: Does the legacy checkout still exist in production?

findings.claim: refund() logs order["id"], which may be absent
findings.failure_scenario: An order dict created without an id is refunded; the log call raises KeyError after the status was already changed.
findings.verdict_reason: The repository has no order constructor, so whether id is always set cannot be checked here.
A negative discount as a surcharge is how the caller in the spec uses it; not a defect.
